title: Grateful Dead Live at Monterey Performing Arts Center on 1969-06-14
lineage: Joel Pollack's DAT (Tascam DA-40)> Tascam DA-3000 > .wav 16/48
source: Bear’s Master Soundboard Cassettes (Ampex C90) > Dick Latvala's 1st generation cassettes (Tascam 122mkIII deck)(TDK SA-X 100) > Joel Pollack's DAT (16/48)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard upgrade captures a psychedelic Lovelight “meltdown,” delivering crystal‑clear, lossless audio with vivid analog vibes.
ai_review.review: The new FLAC version is praised as a major improvement over earlier releases – the soundboard source is crisp, lossless and free of the pitch problems that plagued other versions.  Musically the show shines especially during the first “Lovelight,” where reviewers describe a Coltrane‑like vortex that spirals back into Pigpen’s gritty R&B groove, making it a standout moment.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers gave high marks (5★ and 4★) and highlighted superb audio quality plus a memorable performance, though only two reviews limits confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Lossless FLAC upgrade; clear, crisp mix with no pitch or speed issues noted in earlier releases.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set builds into a psychedelic peak during the first Lovelight, delivering a trancelike vortex before resolving back to Pigpen’s R&B groove – a strong, flowing highlight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned as wanting to capture an analog representation of the psychedelic experience; his vision is reflected in the “meltdown” vibe.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s R&B groove during the Lovelight meltdown is highlighted, showcasing his keyboard/harmonica presence.
